Power Management Strategy of a PV Integrated Microgrid coupled with Hybrid Energy Storage System

Abstract:

The depletion of natural resources and the uncertainty of renewable energy resources have paved the way for the adaptation for a clean renewable resources-based generation and load supply. Microgrid has lower electricity costs through local power management and reduced transmission cost, minimizing the overall shortcomings and increases the reliability of the system. However, the uncoordinated power flow in the microgrid lead to inefficient utilization of energy sources connected to the renewable source. The coordinated and controlled power flow along with the power management between the source, Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) and the load can be achieved by employing a power management control technique. Therefore, with coordinated and bidirectional power flow capability the Modified Droop Control Technique deals with power exchange from the PV source or each energy storage devices to the load. Considering a hybrid energy storage system coupled with PV as the renewable source effectual power exchange, bus voltage restoration and maintaining the appropriate levels of state of charge (SoC) of the HESS are pertinent issues to be addressed. This research work presents the design, control and power management between the source, HESS and the load. The Modified Mixed Droop Technique (MMDT) is a decentralized method for proper power sharing, maintaining constant bus voltage and SoC levels for PV-integrated HESS. MMDT consists of a Virtual Resistance Droop (implemented on battery) which mitigates the low frequency power variations and a Virtual Capacitance Droop (implemented on supercapacitor) which mitigates high frequency power variations. In the process, the bus voltage is maintained at a constant value and SoC of the supercapacitor is maintained at the permissible level. Thus, effectual power exchange, bus voltage regulation, constant power supply to the load, frequency stability and power quality improvement is achieved through the implementation of Modified Mixed Droop Technique (MMDT). To validate the controller for PV-integrated HESS, its designed model is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink platform. The simulation results of a MMDT controller along with power management, DC bus voltage regulation and SoC restoration to its nominal value are showcased for a 0.5 KW PV-HESS system. The developed system can be further explored using the deadbeat control technique and achieving bidirectional power flow among the source, HESS, load and the grid
